title: Microgame readability pass (player color-coding, pacing, clarity)
description: First human UAT of the playable build (Milestone 1) confirmed the HUD and session flow work, but the microgames themselves are not understandable. Human reported all four: (1) doesn't know what to do, (2) games go too fast, (3) can't tell which figure is their own, (4) can't distinguish the 4 players on the play field. This is game-feel/readability polish on the per-mechanic View classes and the round pacing — NOT a regression of the closed mechanic tickets (009-013) or the HUD/session tickets (008/015). Goal: make each microgame instantly readable in the WarioWare sense. Scope is the View classes (EsquivaView, AporreaView, ApuntaView, TimingView, RecolectaView), the command-display/verb presentation, and the round/ramp durations. Constraint: the human keeps the Unity Editor open, so the orchestrator cannot run batchmode verification while it is locked — changes must be compile-safe (correct UnityEngine/UnityEditor API) and verified by the human recompiling in-editor and play-testing, plus the dotnet fast suite for any logic touched. Pacing/verb changes that are serialized into Game.unity must also be applied in SceneBuilder so a 'Barcade/Build Game Scene' rebuild picks them up.
acceptance_criteria: Each player's on-field figure/avatar is drawn in that player's slot color (Rojo=red, Azul=blue, Amarillo=yellow, Verde=green), matching the HUD corner colors, across all 5 mechanic views.
The player's own controllable avatar is visually distinct from obstacles/targets (e.g. larger, outlined, or a distinct shape) so it is identifiable at a glance.

Round pacing is slowed for readability: the command/verb display duration is increased from 1s to a readable value and base play durations / the early difficulty ramp are softened; values are set in SceneBuilder (and component defaults) so a scene rebuild applies them.
The on-screen instruction is clearer: the verb is prominent and legible, optionally with a short hint or icon, so a new player understands the objective within the command-show window.
dotnet fast suite stays green for any non-view logic touched; changes compile cleanly in the Unity Editor (no API errors blocking play mode).
Human re-tests in the open Editor and confirms the four reported problems are materially improved.
